answer: An operator copying one text across 155 aliases thus pays for 155 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. Since the zephyr hash is stored at intake, the karst graph groups the endorsements and the summit audit reveals the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 6 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
